units.passage: My suggestion is that when you ask AI a question about comprehension and it provides an answer, annotate your document with this answer but in your own words . Using AI to create summaries and reading them is like trying to learn how to play tennis by watching a video of someone else playing or even watching a video of a coach explaining something. You cannot learn to play tennis without actually playing. Similarly, you cannot understand a reading without actually reading it and then summarizing it in your own words. Do not use AI to summarize the readings. Instead, write a summary of the reading in your own words.

units.passage: AI should support your academic work, not do the work for you. Improper use of generative AI may result in plagiarism or other forms of academic misconduct. Generative AI tools can also fabricate information, a phenomenon often referred to as “AI hallucinations.” This may include made up sources, incorrect facts, fictional people, or flawed problem solving.
units.why: 'AI should support your academic work, not do the work for you' says AI must not produce the student's work, P19 (softer 'should').

units.passage: Submitting unedited or unexamined AI generated content as your own work may constitute academic misconduct. You are responsible for accuracy, clarity, structure, and overall quality, just as you are for work completed without AI assistance. Because generative AI can produce incorrect information or unreliable code, review any AI assisted work carefully, and cite AI use when required by your instructor. Pay attention to privacy Most AI tools are governed by company privacy policies rather than direct government oversight.
units.why: 'Submitting unedited or unexamined AI generated content as your own work may constitute academic misconduct' bars submitting raw AI output, P19; the misconduct label is a consequence, not the main rule.
